## Your steering: glab CLI, not the API

- `skills/review/gitlab.md` rewritten around `glab` subcommands: `glab mr view`, `glab mr diff`, `glab mr note list`, and `glab mr note create` with `--draft`, `--file`, `--line`, `--old-line`. `--file` targets the latest diff version, so the review never resolves commit SHAs.
- Deleted the whole raw-REST section — the `position[base_sha]/[head_sha]/[start_sha]/[new_path]/[new_line]` form-field fallback and the `/versions` SHA lookup are gone.
- **One `glab api` call survives, and I could not remove it:** `glab api --method POST "projects/:fullpath/merge_requests/<n>/draft_notes/bulk_publish"`. `glab`'s `mr` command has no publish subcommand (its list is approve, approvers, checkout, close, create, delete, diff, issues, list, merge, note, rebase, reopen, revoke, subscribe, todo, unsubscribe, update, view; `mr note` has create, delete, list, reopen, resolve, update). Without it, drafts cannot be published and every finding posts as its own notification. The file says plainly that this is the one place `glab api` is needed, and gives the un-batched alternative. Say the word if you would rather drop batching than keep that call.

## Publishing check (`scripts/check-skill-sync.ts`)

- `SkillSyncPair` is gone. `PublishedSkill` has optional `source`/`sourceHash` plus `supportFiles: {path, hash}[]`; drift matches by `skill`, so a skill with no Agent Definition records and validates. Baseline key renamed `pairs` → `skills`.
- New `collectPublishedSkillFiles(rootPath, skillPath)` reads the skill's Markdown from disk, and `import.meta.main` uses it for both the leak scan and the hashing — a file added to a published skill directory is scanned on the first run, no baseline edit.
- **Beyond the plan's letter:** it recurses into subdirectories rather than reading the directory flat, so a future `skills/review/references/x.md` is covered. A flat read left the same hole one level down.
- `formatDrift` names the path for a changed, unregistered, or missing support file.

## The skill (`skills/review/`, four files)

- `SKILL.md` — target resolution (pull request / fixed point / dirty tree / ask), the seven-rung spec ladder ending in an explicit free-form fallback, both axes with their briefs, and the judgment discipline ported from the Reviewer prompt. No `review_diff`, `review_complete`, `issue-tracker.md`, `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`, `gh`, or `glab` — verified by grep.
- Seam rule ported with the verdict you corrected: advisory by default, blocking only when the project documents a seam policy or the seam lets a test pass without running the behavior under test.
- `pull-requests.md` — host discovery, line-vs-summary mapping, batching, verdict, never approve, confirm before submit. Names the two host files, carries no vendor command.
- `github.md` — `gh` read commands and the batched `gh api --method POST .../pulls/<n>/reviews` with `comments[]`. Confirmed against `gh` 2.100.0 that `gh pr review` has only `--approve/--request-changes/--comment` and cannot attach line comments.
- Registered in the baseline with no `source` and three support files; `skills/README.md` gains the `review` row and explains source-less skills and whole-directory tracking.

## Verification

- `deno task ci` — **exit 0**, full suite, including `seams:check` (0 seams, unchanged) and `skills:sync:check` (3 published skills). That run predates the GitLab rewrite; since then only `gitlab.md` and its baseline hash changed, so I re-ran every check that reads them: `skills:sync:check` green, `check-skill-sync.test.ts` green, `deno fmt --check` clean over 9 files.
- Test count **11 → 17**. No test deleted. All 11 originals survive: 9 unchanged or fixture-updated, 2 renamed as their subject widened (`…in sync with what they were last reviewed against`; `every file the committed skills ship carries none of it`, which now walks every shipped file, not just SKILL.md). One assertion in `both sides moving is still reported` narrowed from whole-object to the two fields it is about, because the drift object grew three fields that test does not care about.
- **The check that proves the check:** appended `RunWield owns this file.` to `skills/review/github.md` → `skills:sync:check` exits 1 naming `skills/review/github.md: RunWield product name "RunWield"`. Reverted → green. Added empty `skills/review/scratch.md` → drift naming it unrecorded. Removed → green.
- **Mutation-tested the new behaviors.** Making `collectPublishedSkillFiles` return only the SKILL.md kills 2 tests; dropping the support-file terms from the drift condition kills 3. Both restored.
- **Seam verdict, on a real fixture:** built a throwaway repo with no standards docs and a commit introducing `const write = deps?.write ?? writeToDisk`. Neither blocking condition applies, so it lands as an advisory. The rule ported, and did not port hot.

## Not verified, and why

- **PR path against a live pull request.** Needs a real PR you nominate; I pointed the skill at nothing and posted nothing.
- **`npx skills@latest add gandazgul/runwield`.** The four files are uncommitted, so the remote has nothing to offer yet.
- **GitLab commands end to end.** `glab` is not installed here. Checked against the current `glab` command reference; the file says documentation-verified.
- **Spec ladder rung 6.** The plan predicted a `HEAD~3` review would reach "ask the user". It reaches rung 5, because `docs/plans/publish-review-skill.md` matches the branch name — the ladder working correctly. Rung 6 is unreachable in this repo.
